entries.subject: DAMIT 1837: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-1837.txt. Model 1837, version 2017-09-21, pole (304°, -41°), period 18.5538 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 154 ±15 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the documented physical calibration supplies the selected scale. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 126.89 ± 1.64 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 146 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.subject: Viikinkoski et al. (2017), AO and light-curve shape models
entries.finding: [Viikinkoski et al. (2017), AO and light-curve shape models](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1708.05191) — retained primary publication; see the body-specific selection and calibration above.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 164, pole ['305', '-41'], [Model 164](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/164) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 164: pole (305°, -41°), 18.5539 h, version 2008-08-27, archive diameter 119 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.
